pairs: Fecit et altare holocausti de lignis setim,
He also made the altar of holocaust from setim wood:
quinque cubitorum per quadrum,
five cubits square,
et trium in altitudine:
and three in height,
cujus cornua de angulis procedebant,
the horns of which proceeded from the corners.
operuitque illum laminis æneis.
And he covered it with layers of brass.
Et in usus ejus paravit ex ære vasa diversa,
And for its uses, he prepared diverse vessels out of brass:
lebetes,
kettles,
forcipes,
forceps,
fuscinulas,
little hooks,
uncinos,
larger hooks,
et ignium receptacula.
and receptacles for the fire.
Craticulamque ejus in modum retis fecit æneam,
And he made its grating of brass, in the manner of a net,
et subter eam in altaris medio arulam,
and under it, in the midst of the altar, its base,
fusis quatuor annulis per totidem retiaculi summitates,
casting four rings at the four ends of the net in order to set the bars,
ad immittendos vectes ad portandum:
so as to carry it.
quos et ipsos fecit de lignis setim,
These bars he also made of setim wood,
et operuit laminis æneis:
and he covered them with layers of brass.
induxitque in circulos,
And he drew them through the rings,
qui in lateribus altaris eminebant.
which projected from the sides of the altar.
Ipsum autem altare non erat solidum,
But the altar itself was not solid,
sed cavum ex tabulis,
but hollow,
et intus vacuum.
made from panels and empty inside.
Fecit et labrum æneum cum basi sua de speculis mulierum,
He also made the washtub of brass,
quæ excubabant in ostio tabernaculi.
with its base made from the mirrors of the women who kept watch at the door of the tabernacle.
Fecit et atrium,
He also made the atrium,
in cujus australi plaga erant tentoria de bysso retorta, cubitorum centum,
at the south side of which were hangings of fine twisted linen of one hundred cubits and
columnæ æneæ viginti cum basibus suis,
twenty columns of brass with their bases.
capita columnarum, et tota operis cælatura, argentea.
The heads of the columns and all of the engraving work were of silver.
Æque ad septentrionalem plagam tentoria columnæ, basesque et capita columnarum ejusdem mensuræ, et operis ac metalli, erant.
Equally, at the northern area, the hangings, the columns, and the bases and heads of the columns were of the same measure and work and metal.
In ea vero plaga, quæ ad occidentem respicit,
Yet truly, on that side which looks out toward the west,
fuerunt tentoria cubitorum quinquaginta,
there were hangings of fifty cubits,
columnæ decem cum basibus suis æneæ,
and ten columns with their bases of brass.
et capita columnarum, et tota operis cælatura, argentea.
And the heads of the columns and all of the engraving work were of silver.
Porro contra orientem quinquaginta cubitorum paravit tentoria:
Furthermore, toward the east, he prepared hangings of fifty cubits:
e quibus,
of which,
quindecim cubitos columnarum trium,
there were fifteen cubits,
cum basibus suis,
among three columns with their bases,
unum tenebat latus:
holding up one side,
et in parte altera (quia inter utraque introitum tabernaculi fecit) quindecim æque cubitorum erant tentoria,
and on the other side, (for between the two he made the entrance of the tabernacle) there were equally hangings of fifteen cubits,
columnæque tres,
and three pillars,
et bases totidem.
and the same number of bases.
Cuncta atrii tentoria byssus retorta texuerat.
All the hangings of the atrium were woven from fine twisted linen.
Bases columnarum fuere æneæ,
The bases of the columns were of brass,
capita autem earum cum cunctis cælaturis suis argentea:
but their heads with all of their engravings were of silver.
sed et ipsas columnas atrii vestivit argento.
Now he also overlaid the columns of the atrium themselves with silver.
Et in introitu ejus opere plumario fecit tentorium ex hyacintho,
And he made, at its entrance, a hanging,
purpura, vermiculo,
wrought with embroidery,
ac bysso retorta,
of hyacinth, purple,
quod habebat viginti cubitos in longitudine,
vermillion, and fine twisted linen, which held twenty cubits in length,
altitudo vero quinque cubitorum erat juxta mensuram, quam cuncta atrii tentoria habebant.
yet truly it was five cubits in height, as with the measure of all the hangings of the atrium.
Columnæ autem in ingressu fuere quatuor cum basibus æneis,
Now the columns at the entrance were four,
capitaque earum
with bases of brass,
et cælaturæ argenteæ.
and their heads and engravings were of silver.
Paxillos quoque tabernaculi
Likewise,
et atrii per gyrum fecit æneos.
the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the atrium all around he made of brass.
Hæc sunt instrumenta tabernaculi testimonii, quæ enumerata sunt juxta præceptum Moysi in cæremoniis Levitarum per manum Ithamar filii Aaron sacerdotis:

These are the instruments of the tabernacle of the testimony, which were enumerated according to the instruction of Moses, with the ceremonies of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest,
quæ Beseleel filius Uri filii Hur de tribu Juda,
which Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur from the tribe of Judah,
Domino per Moysen jubente, compleverat,
had completed, just as the Lord decreed through Moses.
juncto sibi socio Ooliab filio Achisamech de tribu Dan:
He was joined by his associate, Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach,
qui et ipse artifex lignorum egregius fuit,
from the tribe of Dan, who himself was also an exceptional artisan of wood,
et polymitarius atque plumarius ex hyacintho,
and of weaving, as well as of embroidery, with hyacinth,
purpura,
purple,
vermiculo et bysso.
vermillion, and fine linen.
Omne aurum quod expensum est in opere sanctuarii,
All of the gold that was expended in the work of the Sanctuary,
et quod oblatum est in donariis,
and that was offered in donation,
viginti novem talentorum fuit,
was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels,
et septingentorum triginta siclorum ad mensuram sanctuarii.
according to the measure of the Sanctuary.
Oblatum est autem ab his qui transierunt ad numerum a viginti annis et supra,
Now it was offered by those who were past the numbering of twenty years and above:
de sexcentis tribus millibus et quingentis quinquaginta armatorum.
from six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men able to bear arms.
Fuerunt præterea centum talenta argenti e quibus conflatæ sunt bases sanctuarii, et introitus, ubi velum pendet.
There were, beyond that, one hundred talents of silver, from which were cast the bases for the Sanctuary and for the entrance where the veil hangs.
Centum bases factæ sunt de talentis centum,
One hundred bases were made from one hundred talents,
singulis talentis per bases singulas supputatis.
a single talent being counted for each base.
De mille autem septingentis et septuaginta quinque,
But from one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five,
fecit capita columnarum,
he made the heads of the columns,
quas et ipsas vestivit argento.
which he also clothed with silver.
Æris quoque oblata sunt talenta septuaginta duo millia,
Likewise, of brass, there was offered seventy-two thousand talents,
et quadringenti supra sicli,
and four hundred more shekels,
ex quibus fusæ sunt bases in introitu tabernaculi testimonii,
from which were cast the bases at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony,
et altare æneum cum craticula sua,
and the altar of brass with its grating,
omniaque vasa quæ ad usum ejus pertinent,
and the vessels which pertain to its use,
et bases atrii tam in circuitu quam in ingressu ejus,
and the bases of the atrium,
et paxilli tabernaculi
as much at the circumference as at its entrance,
atque atrii per gyrum.
and the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the atrium all round.
